findings.summary: isPublished(articles.get(match[1])) crashes the entire build with a TypeError whenever a /blog/<slug> link points at a slug that isn't in the articles map (typo, renamed file, or since-deleted post) — Map.get returns undefined, and isPublished (line 32) immediately does article.draft on it. Verified by feeding the plugin a synthetic tree with a link to /blog/this-slug-does-not-exist: it throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading draft)' instead of warning/handling gracefully. The repo already has ~12 internal /blog/ links across articles, so a single future typo or slug rename turns into a full production build failure rather than a dead link.

findings.summary: Implementer report states 'Tests for the change were written and run,' but the diff adds no test file (confirmed via repo-wide glob for the plugin name), and neither package.json (root or apps/web) defines any test script or test runner dependency — there is no test infrastructure in this project at all. The claim is false. I ran the real build myself as verification: the happy path (existing draft-linked posts) works and prints correct per-file warnings, but that only surfaces because current content happens to have no broken slug — the crash above went completely undetected.

findings.summary: parseFrontmatter hand-rolls frontmatter extraction with regexes (block boundaries, draft flag, date) instead of using gray-matter, which is already a project devDependency used for the identical job (parsing frontmatter out of these same articles) in scripts/generate-og-images.mjs. The regex approach is more fragile against valid YAML variance (e.g. block/flow style differences) that gray-matter already handles correctly.

findings.summary: Comment claims this 'Mirrors apps/web/src/utils/data-utils.ts,' but the real isPublished bypasses the future-date check when import.meta.env.DEV is true (so authors can preview scheduled posts in dev listings). This plugin's isPublished (line 32) never bypasses the date check, so in `pnpm dev` a link to a soon-to-publish post could get stripped even though the site's own index/tag listings would show that same post as published. Production builds are unaffected since DEV is always false there.
